title: Cohort Price Cushion & HC Allocation — Sprint Scenarios
summary: Sprint-level working worksheet that ties cohort-segmented price cushions to headcount allocation (ops/on-call/devs) across three candidate scenarios. Intended to produce a near-term, operationalizable plan for the next 12 weeks that preserves SLA margin while minimizing incremental FTE spend. This doc is intentionally a working sheet: contains quick assumptions, scenario-level P&L deltas, and recommended triggers for switching between scenarios.
assumptions: 1) Baseline ARR cohort mix: startups 45%, scale-ups 35%, enterprise 20%. 2) Token intensity distribution: startups 60% low-intensity, scale-ups 40% mid, enterprise 25% high. 3) GPU spot pricing volatility +/- 18% over 12 weeks. 4) Headcount hiring lead time = 8 weeks; contractor onboarding = 2 weeks. 5) Burst GPU reserved pool costs are charged to 'capacity buffer' line; can be scaled weekly. 6) We treat price cushion as an ex-ante discount/rebate reserve (liability) sized against cohort churn and unit economics deterioration. 7) All currency USD; rounding to nearest thousand for planning.

scenario_analysis: Conservative: minimal hiring, relies on strict caching/quantization tuning push from infra — small revenue upside, positive margin because we avoid hiring; risk if spot pricing spikes. Balanced: moderate hiring smooths ticket backlog and reduces error SLA penalties; revenue upside driven by ability to serve higher token customers with improved routing; margin still positive but requires capacity buffer. Aggressive: aims to capture high-intensity enterprise usage by raising effective capacity and larger price cushion; short-term margin hit due to hiring and bigger reserved pool, but positions for higher retention and larger contract renewal value.
headcount_rationale:
- Ops FTEs: justify on 8-12 week sprints to reduce MTTI and incident drag; each ops FTE estimated to prevent $40k in SLA penalties per quarter when paired with improved runbooks.
- Infra Dev: one headcount to accelerate kernel tuning and continuous batching improvements expected to reduce per-token GPU cost by ~6% after Q1 of work.
- Billing/Sales Ops: half-FTE contractor to implement cohort gating and credit rules; reduces abusive low-margin volume.
Hiring phasing: Balanced scenario recommends contractor immediate (2w) + hire ops FTE with 8w lead. Aggressive starts contractors + two hires concurrently (8w lead).
sensitivity_observations:
1) A 10% adverse movement in spot GPU pricing reduces net margin under Aggressive scenario by ~14k$ per week unless we throttle startup cohorts.
2) If startup cohort share falls 10pp to 35%, Balanced scenario revenue upside compresses by ~7k$; hiring becomes marginal.
3) Restricting burst pool reduces near-term costs but increases incident risk with high-impact enterprise jobs.
4) Quantization and caching suggestions from infra could shift Balanced to Conservative economics if realized within 6 weeks.
